title: Our Sky

standard_text: The day and night sky: the Sun, the Moon and the stars; day and night and why the Sun seems to move; the changing shapes of the Moon; constellations and the Pole Star; clouds and rainbows; India in space (summary of NCERT Our Wondrous World Chapter 10).

key_big: Earth spins, giving us day and night.
key_sub: The Moon shines with sunlight and changes shape.
body_html:
How to think about it

In the day sky we see the Sun, clouds and sometimes a rainbow. The Sun is the nearest star. Earth spins once in about 24 hours, so the Sun seems to rise in the east and set in the west, and we get day and night. At night we see stars, constellations such as the Saptarishi, and the Pole Star, which shows the north.

The Moon has no light of its own; it reflects sunlight. From Amavasya (new Moon) it grows to Purnima (full Moon) in about 15 days and shrinks again, repeating every 29 to 30 days. ISRO sent Chandrayaan-3 to the Moon in 2023.

Example

The Moon shines because…

no light of its own

Answer: it reflects sunlight

Example

About 15 days after Amavasya…

the Moon grows

Answer: full Moon (Purnima)

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the Sun moves around Earth each day.
  • Calling the Moon a star.
  • Thinking stars disappear in the day.

faq.q: Why do we have day and night?
faq.a: Earth spins; the side facing the Sun has day and the other side has night.

faq.q: Why does the Moon change shape?
faq.a: We see different amounts of its sunlit half as it goes around Earth.

items.q: Which sky sight is caused by sunlight shining through raindrops?
items.e: A rainbow: caused by sunlight shining through raindrops.

items.q: Which of these is not seen in the day sky?
items.e: The Pole Star: not seen in the day sky. The other three are.

items.q: Which of these is seen in the day sky?
items.e: A jet's white trail: seen in the day sky.

items.q: Which of these is not seen in the night sky?
c: a satellite moving like a slow dot of light
items.e: A jet's white trail: not seen in the night sky. The other three are.

items.q: Which of these is seen in the night sky?
items.e: The Pole Star: seen in the night sky.

items.q: Which sky sight is caused by sunlight passing through a lot of air near the horizon?
items.e: A red-orange sky at sunset: caused by sunlight passing through a lot of air near the horizon.

items.q: Which of these is true about a rainbow in the sky?
c: made of tiny water drops in cool air near the ground
caused by sunlight passing through a lot of air near the horizon
caused by sunlight shining through raindrops
caused by thin, high clouds made of ice
items.e: A rainbow: caused by sunlight shining through raindrops.

items.q: Which of these is true about dark, heavy clouds in the sky?
c: made of tiny water drops in cool air near the ground
a sign that rain may come soon
caused by thin, high clouds made of ice
caused by sunlight shining through raindrops
items.e: Dark, heavy clouds: a sign that rain may come soon.

items.q: Which of these is not seen in the night sky?
items.e: A rainbow: not seen in the night sky. The other three are.

items.q: Which of these is seen in the night sky?
items.e: Fireflies near the trees: seen in the night sky.

items.q: Which sky sight is caused by thin, high clouds made of ice?
items.e: A ring (halo) around the Moon: caused by thin, high clouds made of ice.

items.q: Which of these is seen in the night sky?
items.e: A shooting star (meteor): seen in the night sky.

items.q: Which of these is seen in the night sky?

items.e: A satellite moving like a slow dot of light: seen in the night sky.

items.q: Which of these is not seen in the day sky?
items.e: Fireflies near the trees: not seen in the day sky. The other three are.

items.q: Which sky sight is a sign that rain may come soon?
items.e: Dark, heavy clouds: a sign that rain may come soon.

items.q: Which of these is seen in the day sky?
c: the Milky Way on a very dark night
items.e: A hot-air balloon: seen in the day sky.

items.q: Which of these is not seen in the night sky?
items.e: A blue sky: not seen in the night sky. The other three are.

items.q: Which of these is true about thick morning fog in the sky?
c: caused by thin, high clouds made of ice
a sign that rain may come soon
made of tiny water drops in cool air near the ground
caused by sunlight passing through a lot of air near the horizon
items.e: Thick morning fog: made of tiny water drops in cool air near the ground.

items.q: Which of these is seen in the day sky?
c: a satellite moving like a slow dot of light
items.e: A rainbow: seen in the day sky.

items.q: Which of these is seen in the night sky?
c: the Milky Way on a very dark night
items.e: The Milky Way on a very dark night: seen in the night sky.

items.q: Why do we see the Sun rise in the east and set in the west?
c: the Sun jumps across the sky
Earth spins from west to east
the Sun moves around Earth every day
items.e: One spin takes 24 hours.

items.q: Which planet do we live on?
items.e: It is the third planet from the Sun.

items.q: When do we see a rainbow?
c: when the Sun shines while it is raining or just after rain
items.e: Stand with your back to the Sun.

items.q: Why can we not see stars during the day?
c: stars go away in the day
the bright sunlight hides their faint light
items.e: Stars are always there.

items.q: Which of these is the largest planet in our solar system?
items.e: Jupiter: the largest planet in our solar system.

items.q: What is an artificial satellite?
c: Earth's natural satellite that shines by reflecting sunlight
a machine sent by people to go around Earth
the largest planet in our solar system
items.e: An artificial satellite: a machine sent by people to go around Earth.

items.q: What is a constellation?
c: a streak of light made by a small rock burning up in the air
the largest planet in our solar system
a group of stars that seems to make a pattern
a star that gives us light and heat
items.e: A constellation: a group of stars that seems to make a pattern.

items.q: How long does Earth take to spin once?
items.e: This gives one day and night.

items.q: What is the Sun?
c: a star that gives us light and heat
a star that stays in the northern sky
the largest planet in our solar system
the planet with bright rings around it
items.e: The Sun: a star that gives us light and heat.

items.q: Which of these is a star that stays in the northern sky?
items.e: The Pole Star (Dhruva Tara): a star that stays in the northern sky.

items.q: Which instrument helps us see far-off stars and planets clearly?
items.e: Galileo used one to see Jupiter's moons.

items.q: Which Indian mission landed near the south pole of the Moon in 2023?
items.e: Its lander was named Vikram.

items.q: What is Mars?
c: our galaxy, a huge group of billions of stars
the largest planet in our solar system
a group of stars that seems to make a pattern
items.e: Mars: the red planet.

items.q: Which of these is the planet with bright rings around it?
items.e: Saturn: the planet with bright rings around it.

items.q: Why do we see more stars in a village than in a big city?
c: there are no stars over cities
city lights and pollution make the sky too bright
items.e: This is light pollution.

items.q: What is the Saptarishi?
c: a group of seven bright stars in the northern sky
items.e: It is also called the Big Dipper.

items.q: What is a meteor (shooting star)?
c: a streak of light made by a small rock burning up in the air
the planet with bright rings around it
a machine sent by people to go around Earth
items.e: A meteor (shooting star): a streak of light made by a small rock burning up in the air.

items.q: Which of these is a group of stars that seems to make a pattern?
items.e: A constellation: a group of stars that seems to make a pattern.

items.q: Why do we have day and night?
c: Earth spins, so one side faces the Sun and the other side is in darkness
the Moon covers the Sun every night
items.e: Day is on the side facing the Sun.

items.q: When is your shadow shortest on a sunny day?
items.e: The Sun is highest then.

items.q: After Purnima the Moon shrinks each night. Which shape comes just after the thin crescent?
items.e: Full → nearly full → half → crescent → new.

items.q: After Amavasya the Moon grows each night. Which shape comes just after the thin crescent?
items.e: New → crescent → half → nearly full → full.

items.q: After Amavasya the Moon grows each night. Which shape comes just after the nearly full Moon?
items.e: New → crescent → half → nearly full → full.

items.q: Why does the Moon look different on different nights?
c: we see different amounts of its sunlit half
items.e: These are the phases of the Moon.

items.q: What is the name for the night of the full Moon?
items.e: Purnima: the night of the full Moon.

items.q: In which direction does your shadow fall in the morning?
items.e: The Sun is in the east in the morning.

items.q: After Amavasya the Moon grows each night. Which shape comes just after the half Moon?
items.e: New → crescent → half → nearly full → full.

items.q: Arjun sees a full Moon (Purnima) tonight. About 29 days later, what will the Moon look like?
items.e: The Moon repeats its shapes about every 29 to 30 days.

items.q: Meera sees no Moon at all on Amavasya. About 15 days later, what will the Moon look like?
items.e: The full Moon comes about 15 days after the new Moon.

items.q: After Purnima the Moon shrinks each night. Which shape comes just after the half Moon?
items.e: Full → nearly full → half → crescent → new.

items.q: Aditya sees a half Moon tonight. About 29 days later, what will the Moon look like?
items.e: The Moon repeats its shapes about every 29 to 30 days.

items.q: Why can we see the Moon during the day sometimes?
c: it is bright enough to be seen when it is above the horizon
the Sun turns into the Moon
items.e: Look for it in the morning or afternoon.

items.q: After Purnima the Moon shrinks each night. Which shape comes just after the nearly full Moon?
items.e: Full → nearly full → half → crescent → new.

items.q: Priya sees no Moon at all on Amavasya. About 14 days later, what will the Moon look like?
items.e: The full Moon comes about 15 days after the new Moon.

items.q: What is the name for the night when the Moon cannot be seen (new moon)?
items.e: Amavasya: the night when the Moon cannot be seen (new moon).

items.q: What is the waning Moon?
c: the night of the full Moon
the night when the Moon cannot be seen (new moon)
the Moon looking smaller each night after Purnima
the Moon looking bigger each night after Amavasya
items.e: The waning Moon: the Moon looking smaller each night after Purnima.

items.q: What is the name for the Moon looking smaller each night after Purnima?
items.e: The waning Moon: the Moon looking smaller each night after Purnima.

items.q: What is the Indian space agency called?
items.e: It is based in Bengaluru.

items.q: What is Amavasya?
c: the night when the Moon cannot be seen (new moon)
the Moon looking bigger each night after Amavasya
the Moon looking smaller each night after Purnima
the night of the full Moon
items.e: Amavasya: the night when the Moon cannot be seen (new moon).

items.q: Aditya sees a thin crescent tonight. About 29 days later, what will the Moon look like?
items.e: The Moon repeats its shapes about every 29 to 30 days.

items.q: What is the Moon?
c: Earth's natural satellite that shines by reflecting sunlight
the largest planet in our solar system
a group of stars that seems to make a pattern
a star that stays in the northern sky
items.e: The Moon: Earth's natural satellite that shines by reflecting sunlight.

items.q: Which of these describes Mangalyaan?
c: the mission that landed near the south pole of the Moon in 2023
the mission sent in 2023 to study the Sun
items.e: Mangalyaan: India's first mission to Mars.

items.q: What do we call people who study the stars and planets?
items.e: Aryabhata was a great Indian astronomer.

items.q: Which of these is a streak of light made by a small rock burning up in the air?
items.e: A meteor (shooting star): a streak of light made by a small rock burning up in the air.

items.q: Which is the mission that landed near the south pole of the Moon in 2023?
items.e: Chandrayaan-3: the mission that landed near the south pole of the Moon in 2023.

items.q: What is Jupiter?
c: a group of stars that seems to make a pattern
the largest planet in our solar system
a star that stays in the northern sky

items.q: What is the Pole Star (Dhruva Tara)?
c: a star that gives us light and heat
Earth's natural satellite that shines by reflecting sunlight
a star that stays in the northern sky
a streak of light made by a small rock burning up in the air
items.e: The Pole Star (Dhruva Tara): a star that stays in the northern sky.

items.q: How long does Earth take to go once around the Sun?
items.e: This is one year.

items.q: Which is India's mission to send astronauts into space?
items.e: Gaganyaan: India's mission to send astronauts into space.

items.q: How long does the Moon take to go from one full Moon to the next?
items.e: That is about a month.

items.q: Which of these is the red planet?

items.q: Which of these is not seen in the night sky?

items.e: Sunlight shining through clouds: not seen in the night sky. The other three are.

items.q: Why is it hotter at noon than in the early morning?

items.q: Which of these is seen in the day sky?

items.q: Which of these is not seen in the day sky?

items.q: Which of these is true about a red-orange sky at sunset in the sky?

items.q: Which of these is true about a ring (halo) around the Moon in the sky?
